R190-R191.summary: Riario to the Earl of Desmond, Elvas 12 January 1581: the papal fort in Ireland is reported lost; aid is being sought. A news note: the viceroy put the garrison to the sword without resistance. A memorial to Philip II on the Italian infantry (3,037 paid, about 1,000 fit), the offer of 2,000 under the Pope's name for 4 months, and a commissary to hand them to Desmond.
R190-R191.en:
I have heard with great satisfaction how valiantly Your Lordship bears the charge there {of His Holiness's soldiers},
and how you do not cease to take the best care of them and to make what progress is possible. Thanking you warmly
for this, for the service of God, which is pursued with infinite zeal {by His Beatitude}, I tell you that here no
effort has been spared to obtain {strong aid} for you; and it has been held back because of the news that has come to
this court {that the fort held by your force has been lost, and part of those soldiers too}. But be assured that every
office is being done with His Holiness and His Majesty so that {notable relief} may be made ready; and meanwhile do not
fail to attend {to the enterprise} with the same valour and vigilance, hoping that I shall always obtain for you from
these two princes all I can to your liking.

R192-R194.summary: Riario to the Secretary, 4-5 January 1581: Philip II thanks the Pope for the warning about the Piedmont plot (Ayamonte, the Anselmi, Huguenots of the Dauphiné) and will not let Italy be disturbed; the English enterprise, the Italian troops and the news that has cooled the ministers. With a copy of 29 November 1580: Flanders first, the Italians embarked at Lisbon offered for Ireland or sent home.
R192-R194.en:
Today, the 4th of January, I spoke to His Majesty {about the Piedmont business}, so that His Majesty was very content and
showed himself much obliged to His Holiness, whose feet he kisses a thousand times for this kind {warning}, {telling me
that there is something in it concerning those Anselmi, putting their men into Italy}; and that he would have {the
letters they had on this business} searched for, and would send Idiáquez to me to inform me of everything, so that I
could {report to His Holiness}; so I shall wait and report what happens. But certainly {His Majesty has taken the
warning in very good part, and the Piedmont affair I believe is true, but I believe it will not turn out wholly to His
Majesty's satisfaction}, who readily has the same {suspicion as His Holiness}.
